correctness.rationale: The 16-vertex GP(8,3) graph is explicitly defined by edge rules. All 40320 bipartite bijections are tested, giving 33 matchings, independently reproduced by recursive exact-cover enumeration. The equivalence of a flip and a single-cycle symmetric difference is proved for any pair of perfect matchings. Two distinct programs enumerate all 528 pairs by symmetric difference, respectively 24 six-cycles plus 30 eight-cycles by DFS with explicit flips, and agree on all 96 and 36 edge pairs as certified by a shared canonical SHA-256. Degree-neighbor identities yield the stated three-hub octagon graph. Complete BFS for all 33 states verifies combined eccentricity three, while elementary distances in the three-hub graph establish octagon diameter four and radius three. The 6-only graph has three isolated states, proving the sharp length-eight threshold. These are exhaustive finite computations with source files supplied, not samples or logs in isolation.

value.rationale: The Möbius–Kantor graph is a classical highly symmetric nonplanar bipartite graph with hexagonal torus embeddings (Marušič–Pisanski 2000). A natural question is whether shortest alternating-cycle moves suffice to make its dimer state space irreducible. They do not: all six-cycle flips leave three frozen states; yet eight-cycle flips *alone* already yield a connected graph with an explicit, unusually simple structural model. The sharp threshold and three-hub/octagon distance geometry answer a mathematically motivated transformability question that is not determined by the previously published count 33 or graph symmetry. This is a complete finite structural classification, not an arbitrary slice or small numerical improvement. Its scope is one fixed graph and no mixing-rate conclusion is claimed.
